A few words about me

Konstantina Mpogiatzi, clinical psychologist in Kalamaria

My therapeutic stance is guided by emotional availability, warmth, empathy and respect for what makes each person unique.

Licence: ΔΔΥΚΜ/Μ.Ε.Θ.526101(15495)/25-08-2021 · verified profile

I am a clinical psychologist with a private practice in Kalamaria. I studied at the School of Psychology of the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, where I also completed my MSc in Clinical Psychology.

My clinical experience has been shaped through steady private practice in individual psychotherapy for adults, and through work with specialised mental health services: the Hellenic Centre for Mental Health and Research (E.KE.PSY.E.), the 2nd University Adult Psychiatric Clinic of the Aristotle University, the Applied Psychology Laboratory of the Aristotle University, the Alzheimer Society (SOPSY) and private specialist therapy centres.

I have completed a two-year training in Cognitive-Behavioural Therapy (CBT) for Children and Adolescents at the Hellenic Association for Behaviour Research (EEES), and I regularly attend further training in trauma, clinical psychopathology and current therapeutic practice. To keep my work at a high standard, I am in continuous training and regular clinical supervision.

The therapeutic relationship

A space to understand yourself

In psychotherapy, the therapeutic relationship is built gradually, with trust, acceptance and respect for your own pace. The aim is to understand more deeply what you are going through, to recognise patterns that make things hard for you, and to discover new ways of facing the challenges in your life.

  • Safety and trust

    A relationship in which you can express yourself freely, without needing to have all the answers.

  • Understanding and change

    We explore what affects the way you feel, think and relate to others.

  • At your own pace

    The course of therapy adapts to your needs, making room for both understanding and change.

The approach

Cognitive-
behavioural psychotherapy

In my work with adults I follow the Cognitive-Behavioural approach (CBT), also drawing on elements of Schema Therapy and psychodynamic theory. We focus on your difficulties and needs in the present, while also keeping your developmental path in mind: how experiences and relationships at each stage of life shape how you see yourself, how you handle emotions and how you relate to others.

«Self-awareness, changing the patterns that make life hard, working through what hurt.»

How thoughts, emotions and behaviours feed each other

Interactive section

The Lenses of Thought: How Do We Interpret the World Around Us?

Our experiences and beliefs shape the “lenses” through which we see ourselves, others and our relationships. Often, in moments of pressure or insecurity, our lens can “blur”, leading us to automatic interpretations that do not necessarily match reality.

Through therapy, we learn to recognise these thinking patterns, to examine our interpretations and to discover more flexible and realistic ways of understanding what happens to us.

Cognitive distortions = Distortions of reality

  • 1Personalisation“Everything is about me.”

    We read other people’s behaviour or mood as the result of something we did, even when we do not have enough evidence.

  • 2Catastrophising“What if the worst happens?”

    We focus on the most negative possible scenario and find it hard to see other possible outcomes.

  • 3“All-or-nothing” thinking“Either perfect or a failure.”

    We judge ourselves and situations in absolute terms, leaving no room for anything in between.

A different view can make a difference.

We don’t need to push ourselves to think positively. We can learn to recognise our automatic thoughts, look at the evidence, and treat ourselves with more understanding and kindness.

Questions

Frequently asked questions

Something else on your mind? Call me — we can talk it through before the first session.

210 744 4147
How long is a session?

Each session lasts 50 minutes, whether in person at the office in Kalamaria or online by video call. We agree on how often to meet together, depending on what you need.

How do I book?

Call 210 744 4147 or book online through doctoranytime, either at the office or by video call. In the first session we get to know each other and talk about what brings you.

Do you offer online sessions?

Yes. Sessions take place in person and online. An online session has the same length and structure, and is a good option if you live far away or have a busy schedule.

Which approach do you use?

With adults I work with Cognitive-Behavioural Therapy (CBT), also drawing on elements of Schema Therapy and psychodynamic theory. We focus on the present, keeping your developmental path in mind.

How do I pay?

You can pay at the office by card or in cash, or online when booking through doctoranytime (Klarna is also available).

Can I cancel an appointment?

Yes, up to 24 hours before the appointment. If you paid online, the money is refunded.

Is there parking?

The office has no parking of its own; if you come by car, allow a little time to find a space in the neighbourhood.

Is everything I say confidential?

Yes. What we discuss stays between us, under the psychologists’ code of ethics — with the only exceptions being those set by law, when there is immediate danger to you or others.
